proposal.quote: The bomber force will probably consist of some 1,500 aircraft, ~eluding 700 BADGERS, 500 BISONS, and 300 BEARS.
proposal.rule: claude backend: The estimate's probable mid-1960 force is 500 BISON plus 300 BEAR heavy bombers, about 800 intercontinental vehicles; medium BADGERs are excluded and no operational ICBM capability is projected for the period, so the total falls in the 200-999 band (the Army dissent argues for a lower figure but the estimate itself projects 800).

proposal.quote: we estimate that the Soviets may by mid-1960 have about 400-600 heavy bombers and tankers of jet and turboprop types
proposal.rule: claude backend: The estimate's projection for about 2.5 years ahead is a mid-range of about 500 heavy bombers and tankers, which the estimate counts together, plus only a few (say 10) prototype ICBMs. That sum falls in the 200-999 band. (also read in 1 other part(s))

proposal.quote: they are unlikely to initiate general war or to pursue courses of action which, in their judgment, gravely risk general war ... the Soviet leaders will probably continue to prefer non-military means of achieving their objectives
proposal.rule: claude backend: Washington reads Soviet aims as expansion by threats, aid and local pressure while avoiding risks of general war, which matches opportunist. Confidence is low because the source is an intelligence estimate rather than a basic national security paper. (also read in 1 other part(s))

proposal.quote: some time duri.ng the period mid1958 to mid-1959, the USSR will probably have a first operational capability with up to 10 prototype ICBMs ... an operational capability with ·100 ICBMs about one year after its first operational capability date, and with 500 ICBMs about two or at most three years after first operational capability date.
proposal.rule: claude backend: Interpolating between the estimate's milestones (first capability around end-1958, 100 ICBMs around end-1959, 500 around mid-1961) gives roughly 230 to 370 ICBMs two to three years after December 1957. That ICBM count alone falls in the 200-999 band; the document gives no bomber or SLBM figures, so the summed total cannot be checked beyond this.
